feed.title: Windhawk Mod Updates
feed.subtitle: Updates in the official collection of Windhawk mods

entry.title: Hide Taskbar Tooltips 1.3.1
entry.content:
• Add hideStartButtonTooltip setting to hide or show the Windows Start button tooltip independently of taskbar applications.
  • Accurately identify the Start button by querying AutomationProperties.AutomationId == L"StartButton" on the ExperienceToggleButton instance, preventing misclassification of the Task View button.
  • Add tooltipHoverDelayMs setting to configure an extra stationary hover delay (in milliseconds) before showing visible tooltips, while keeping hidden tooltip areas permanently suppressed.
  • Fall back to native display behavior if delayed tooltip scheduling fails or when tooltips open on external Explorer threads to prevent them from being swallowed.
  • Disarm delayed tooltip Win32 timers synchronously on the Shell_TrayWnd UI thread using SendMessageW in Wh_ModBeforeUninit to guarantee all timers are killed before the DLL is unloaded (FreeLibrary).
  • Replace heavy C++/WinRT XAML headers with lightweight ABI COM interfaces, cache IVisualTreeHelperStatics once per visual tree walk, and adopt WRL HString / HStringReference to reduce overhead.
  • Clean up unused -lole32 and -loleaut32 compiler options and remove obsolete #undef GetCurrentTime.

entry.title: Taskbar Thumbnail Stats 1.5
entry.content:
• option to measure RAM as private bytes (like System Informer)
  • CPU is now shown before RAM (configurable) and labels use a colon ("CPU: 3.4% · RAM: 412 MB")
  • "N/A" instead of "…" while the CPU usage is being measured

entry.title: Spotlight Launcher 0.7.1
entry.content:
• A chip for every drive. File mode now shows a chip (with a disk icon) for each of your drives on a second row, kept apart from the location chips so the two groups do not read as one list. A chip is added for every fixed and removable drive that is ready; empty card readers, optical drives with no disc and network drives are skipped, so nothing ever raises a "there is no disk" dialog. The row appears only when you have two or more drives (with a single drive there is nothing to switch to). The chips are detected automatically, no setup.
  • A "This PC" drives view. Going up from a drive root — ← or Backspace on an empty box, or Alt + ↑ — now opens a list of all your drives instead of doing nothing, so you can move between drives with the arrows alone. Enter or → opens the highlighted drive; each row shows its label and free space.
  • Location chips follow moved folders. The Home, Downloads, Documents, Pictures, Music and Videos chips now resolve to each folder's real location, so they still work when a folder has been moved to another drive or redirected (for example a OneDrive-backed Documents).
  • Switch drives with Ctrl + Tab. Ctrl + Tab cycles forward through the drive chips and Ctrl + Shift + Tab backward (the six location chips are left out, since they are a separate idea). Ctrl + 1…9 now jumps to any chip — locations first, then drives — and typing a path such as D:\ in the path bar still works.
  • Start drive setting. A new Start drive option (a single drive letter) chooses which drive the file browser opens on the first time you use it in a session. Empty — or a drive that is not available, such as an unplugged USB stick — opens on Home, as before.
  • The F1 cheat sheet and the README shortcut tables list the new keys.
  • The F1 help sheet no longer resets the bar. It now overlays the current view and closing it returns exactly where you were — the same folder and selection in the file browser, or the calculation you were working on — instead of starting over as if the launcher had just opened.

entry.title: Lock Screen Clock Styler 0.5.0
entry.content:
• Added comprehensive localization for 12 new locales (Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Korean, German, Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese, French, Italian, Polish, Russian, Ukrainian) alongside English and Turkish (14 languages total).
  • Increased default digit font size from 92 to 140 for improved readability and prominence on modern displays.
  • Enabled live seconds toggle by default across all supported themes.
  • Streamlined feature overview and reordered screenshots showcase to feature Retro Pixel.
  • Clarified glass opacity setting description specifically for Modern Flip cards.
  • Cleaned up unused compiler flags (-lcomctl32).
  • Added Community Contributing & Feedback guidelines.

entry.title: Mac Island & Dock 2.1.0
entry.content:
Folders

  • Sorting by date now finds the newest files in folders with more than 200 items; wider columns.
  • Sorted as in Explorer (name, date modified, type or size, either way, with the date, type or size shown), only one kind of file shown or folders mixed with the files, and each pin with its own icon and color (with an "Apply" button to close the choice); pinned folders show a folder icon again.
  • A file's row has two buttons: copy the file (pasted in a folder, it goes there) and copy its path (#6161).
  • Windows' places open with a click; their pin, at the row's end, pins them (a click used to pin them, #6161).
  • Favorite files: a star on a file's row keeps it with the pinned folders, where a click opens it and its buttons copy the file or its path; one deleted or moved leaves the list, one on a drive taken out comes back with the drive (up to 40).
  • The pins, their icons and colors and the folders' order are each Windows account's own (another account on the same PC no longer shares them).

Calendar

  • Clicking an upcoming event or holiday shows its day in the calendar (#6156).

Notifications

  • With islands on several monitors, the Monitors section chooses which islands show the notifications (the main one by default). The main island keeps the sounds, Windows' banners, Win+N, and calls, alarms and reminders; opening, deleting or minimizing a notification on one island closes it on the others (#6159).
  • The apps with notifications can fold into an arrow, like the tray: they come out a moment when a notification comes, and under the mouse (an option, #6129, #6204, #6208).
  • Chat apps that only blink their tray icon instead of sending notifications to Windows (the Chinese WeChat, WeCom, DingTalk) show on the pill with their dot when it starts blinking (#6074, #6215).

The pill

  • The time can be turned off (on by default, per profile): the date alone shows then, with its own options as before, or nothing when they're off too.
  • A "Show desktop" button for the control center and the pill (off by default).
  • The language bubble only shows when the app in front changes its own mode (Shift, the indicator), not when another app comes in front, and it's no longer cut with a low pill (#6422).
  • An item drawn in two parts (the battery or the volume and its percentage) has one hover highlight (#6460).
  • Win+J (an option, off by default, #6519) minimizes the islands to their line and brings them back; its keys can be changed by recording them in the settings (a click, then the new keys; Win+J back with one click), with a warning when Windows or another app uses them too.
  • With notches, the keyboard language bubble shows once, from the middle notch (#6199).
  • What's playing's note, its cover and title, and its buttons are three items of their own in the pill's order (each placed and turned on or off on its own; current layouts keep them together).
  • A control center button that's on (like night light) shows its icon in the accent color with a dot under it, instead of a white disc behind it.
  • A notification's title too long scrolls under the mouse (#6200).

Media

  • A mixer in the media panel: every app with audio sessions on the default output, one entry per program with its icon, name, volume and mute by clicking the icon; the playing app keeps its own volume and mute in the player, with the device's volume and a button for Windows' mixer below it (Win+Ctrl+V on Windows 11 23H2+, sndvol on older versions or if input fails). The mixer opens collapsed and expands with an animated arrow. The session list and icon conversion are shared with the control center.
  • Source chips show the apps' icons, dimmed when paused, and Automatic has its own glyph. They wrap into more rows when needed.
  • A larger cover, the whole modal tinted from the cover's average color with a smooth color transition, a small app icon beside its name, and two pill switches with rounded highlights in a compact footer; the panel scrolls for long lists and stays within its monitor, with press and spring animations, crossfading/sliding media source transitions and animated mute icons/volume bars.
  • Volume sliders follow the pointer while dragging; audio writes are coalesced off the drawing thread, the mixer reveal keeps its existing row geometry, and footer labels have padding on both sides. Accent colors, media text and icons are cached outside drawing; idle monitor/notch profiles are skipped by the animation loop.
  • Lyrics default to Follows the line (each line's own width, up to 360 DIPs); Short, Medium and Long hold the widest line until a pause or gap.

Credits

  • The README's credits (English and Portuguese) link m417z's mod and ask for credit, with a link, from anyone reusing this mod's code or inspired by it (a request, not a license condition).

New items on the pill (each off by default, #6157)

  • The Recycle Bin: how many items; open it, or empty it with a second click; always shown, or only once what's in it weighs 100 MB, 500 MB, 1 GB or 5 GB.
  • A timer, a stopwatch (with hundredths) and Pomodoro, each on its own (all three can run at once), in a panel like the macOS Clock app: lengths in hours, minutes and seconds on wheels (the mouse wheel, a drag or typed), a ring while it runs, Pomodoro's focus and break chosen; the pill shows the one ending first, in orange, and a click on it lists every one going as Live Activities like the iPhone's (each with its time, Pause and Cancel, the next alarm with its switch, Show all); a notice when each ends, with Repeat and Stop (Pomodoro: Stop and OK); and alarms in the same panel: a time each day on wheels, each on or off, with or without a sound, edited with a pencil, its notice with Stop (its sound repeats until then, a minute at most); alarms ring and timers end on time also behind a full-screen app or while the island restarts, and each Windows account has its own; Control Center buttons for the stopwatch, Pomodoro and alarms (#6156).
  • The network's speed, up and down.
  • An audio visualizer: six rounded bars jumping with the beat of the playing app's own sound (or any sound, like VLC's) while something plays, or swaying smoothly like the iPhone's (an option), with a sensitivity slider and a color (the icons', Windows' accent, a rainbow, your own or the cover's).
  • World clocks: Windows' own additional clocks (Date & time settings), shown as soon as they're added there, with a day ahead or behind marked; a click opens Windows' list of them.
  • The time until the next event, alarm, timer or Pomodoro part (each can be left out; in the next 12 hours); a click opens it.
  • The pill filling like a loading bar (each an option, off by default, in the Animations tab): with the progress apps show on their taskbar button (downloads, copies, installs; #6071, read from the taskbar's own progress bar), and with a laptop's battery charge while it charges (not while it's held at a charge limit, like 80%); one bar across the Fixed style's notches (the whole bar in the Bar style), a solid line under it like the taskbar's; a color for each kind (downloads and other apps, Windows' file copies, the battery: green, blue, Windows' accent or your own; red for an error, yellow paused); it moves simply, as a liquid wave or as a glow with particles; paused it breathes, an error shakes, done flashes with a check, canceled drains back.
  • Song lyrics (an option, off by default, goes online: each song's title and artist are sent to lrclib.net): the line sung now on the pill, in time with the song (its size, color and longest line chosen; or in the song title's place while a line is sung, an option), and all of them in a panel where a line clicked goes there in the song. Only for songs (with an artist, 45 s to 20 min, not videos or voice messages), and "Apps that look for lyrics" lists the apps seen playing as cards with their icons, each one's lyrics turned off with its switch; a search result is taken only when its title, artist and length match.

Status notices (from the pill, an option, off by default)

  • The charger plugged in, the battery under 20% and 10%, a Bluetooth audio device connected, and "Do not disturb" turned on or off (#6158, #6204); on the main island, also when it doesn't show the apps' notifications.

Tray icons

  • The grid of the icons not pinned has its own number of columns (6 as before, #6162).

Languages

  • The island and Windhawk's settings in German, Spanish, Russian and Japanese too (#6472), chosen in the island's settings or like Windows' display language; the dates follow them.

Settings

  • The island's settings open in a window of their own, like Windows' Settings (the gear under the island and the control center's): a side bar with the search and a tab per subject (also Dock, About and Logs), each option on a card with a line saying what it does, the island's preview at the top (its items in their order, dragged to move them), resizable, in the island's colors over Mica. A dimmed option says why under its name, and a click there goes to what it needs. Logs copies or saves a summary, the settings and the island's last 300 log lines without turning on Windhawk's logs.
  • Clearer texts for the two options that hide the clock and the tray (the Windows taskbar's, with the island; the dock's, without it).
  • The Monitors page: where the island appears as three buttons that say what they do, the screens as a bigger map (the islands marked), and with an island on every monitor a card for each (its notifications, its look).
  • One settings window a monitor (a notch opens its monitor's), opened at its own monitor's size, and back where it was after the island starts again.
  • A What's new tab (between About and Logs) with the notes of every published version (2.0.0, 2.0.1, 2.0.6 and 2.1.0) for users, in the island's 7 languages, switched by flags the mod draws itself (Direct2D shapes, nothing downloaded); it opens in the island's language, and the search finds the notes. The language buttons in General show the flags too.
  • Once per version (also on a first install), 10 seconds after the main island starts, a notice from the pill says what's new and stays until one of its buttons opens that tab or closes it (an option, on by default, per profile). The language buttons' flags sit on whole pixels, sharp at 150% and 175% too.

Control center

  • Every pill item that opens something can also be a control center button (hidden until added with Edit): notifications, calendar, what's playing, power, CPU/RAM use, profiles, keyboard language, privacy, USB drives, virtual desktops, folders, wallpaper, komorebi's layout, world clocks, next event, Recycle Bin, timer and the tray icons.
  • The magnifier, the narrator and the new on-screen keyboard are buttons that start them (their state wasn't always read right; the magnifier falls back to Win+Plus when it doesn't start); the on-screen keyboard can also go on the control center and the pill (#6160).

Brightness

  • A laptop's own screen has its slider and wheel too (through WMI, like Windows' own slider), beside monitors with DDC/CI; a monitor without DDC/CI shows none, as before (#6436, #6457, #6501, #6350).
  • The wheel on the brightness adds up small turns (touchpads, smooth wheels) instead of losing them (#6420).

Fixes

  • The island's window no longer reaches 3 pixels into a monitor above its own (it kept that monitor's dock from coming up at the middle of its edge).
  • Panels stay inside their monitor and never as tall as it (a long list went past the screen's bottom, into the next monitor, and Wallpaper Engine took it for a full-screen app and stopped).
  • Win+N and Win+A open on the main island wherever the mouse is; minimizing a notification sets its app aside on every island.
  • Every item on the pill grows in and shrinks away (the tray, the media's parts, the uses, the app in focus, the folders, the minimize button and the percentages used to jump); a group whose contents change size follows them smoothly.
  • The Bar style scrolls through its items when they don't fit; the control center has no limit of eight and grows wider to fit the screen.
  • A notification's app icon missing right after a restart is looked for again within seconds.
  • Closing a virtual desktop from the desktops' list closes that one, also when it's a few desktops away, and goes back to where you were (#6164).
  • The network item no longer shows a cable on Wi-Fi when Windows doesn't give the Wi-Fi's details (#6361).
  • The Task Manager button opens it also with an administrator's window in front (it pressed Ctrl+Shift+Esc, which Windows dropped then).
  • The dock comes up only with the mouse at the screen's bottom edge again; the strip above the edge counts only with another monitor below (#6472).
  • A Windhawk setting chooses the height over the bottom edge that brings the dock (or the transparent taskbar) up (in pixels at 100% scale), the same on every monitor; 0, the default, keeps it automatic (#6472).
  • The minimized line's invisible strip is half as thick: the mouse passing near the edge no longer brings the island back (#6468).
  • The control center's Emoji and Clipboard buttons open for the app in front, instead of closing at once.
  • While a panel opened from the pill is open, the pill keeps its width (a longer or shorter media title scrolls in it) and resizes once the panel closes, so the panel's corners stay put; one wider than the pill closes up before narrowing, so its contents aren't cut at the sides.
  • Right after Windows starts, the progress fill waits 30 seconds (apps restoring themselves reported a progress they didn't have and filled the whole bar).
  • A taskbar button without an app ID for a moment no longer makes its badge blink or loses the taskbar's own picture.
  • The dock no longer shows the plate the taskbar stacks behind an app with more windows, and an overlay picture (like a browser profile's photo) stays sharp at its own size as the icon grows.
  • With the timer's item on the pill, the next event item no longer shows the timer and Pomodoro too.
  • The progress fill reaches into the notches' curves.
  • The progress fill follows only what the taskbar's buttons show, read again every second while it shows (it no longer stays after an app has finished), and a new progress fills the pill after 5 seconds (Windows' file copies at once).
  • The visualizer follows the playing app's loudest audio session (a browser has several), and the output's sound while that app is paused or quiet, instead of staying still.
  • Turning the mod off puts the taskbar's auto-hide back only once Windows confirms it (and tries again later if it didn't), each taskbar button keeps its own app's icon and badge, and one taskbar element failing no longer stops the rest of the cleanup.

entry.title: Quick Launch Dock 1.1.0
entry.content:
• Up to four dock panels (right, left, top, bottom) in any combination, each with its own independent list of programs.
  • Icons can be reordered by pressing and holding an icon and dragging it along the dock, or onto another panel. All panels slide out while you drag.
  • Panel size settings: panel thickness, space around each icon and panel inner padding, set separately from the icon size.
  • Websites can be added as slots from the "Add to the dock" item of the right-click menu, or by pasting a link from the clipboard. A click opens the address in the default browser.
  • Websites get a gray globe icon. The optional "Download site icons" setting (off by default) lets the mod request only the site's own /favicon.ico in the background: a spinner is shown while it downloads and the globe stays if it cannot be downloaded. No third-party servers are contacted.
  • Downloaded site icons that blend in with the panel color get a light or dark backing so they stay visible.
  • Seven animation styles: Slide and pop (default), Jelly, Ripple, Fade, Genie, Oval and Droplet.
  • Added an animation speed setting (default 25%) that applies to every style.
  • Icon magnification under the cursor, like in macOS, works with any animation style.
  • Panel opacity setting (10-100%, the icons stay opaque) and a glass style.
  • Change icon / Reset icon in the right-click menu (PNG, JPG, BMP, GIF, ICO). The choice is remembered.
  • Shortcut icons are taken from the shortcut target, so the shortcut arrow overlay is no longer shown.
  • The "+" slot can be hidden in the settings. Items can still be added by drag and drop or from the "Add to the dock" item of the right-click menu of any icon.
  • The dock lists are now stored separately for every Windows account. The first account that starts this version takes over the list saved by earlier versions.
  • Fixed Chrome not starting and programs launching slowly: programs are now launched through Explorer.
  • Fixed black squares behind icons.
  • The old "Screen side" setting was removed. The list saved by previous versions stays on the right panel, so users who kept the dock on the left will see their list on the right panel.
  • Added an animation refresh rate setting (Auto, 120, 144, 180, 240 or 360 Hz), useful for laptops whose refresh rate changes.
  • Corner radius setting for the panel.
  • "Follow the Windows theme" option: takes light/dark colors and the accent color from Windows and updates when the theme changes.
  • Optional dot on icons of running programs (on by default).
  • Small press effect when you click an icon.

entry.title: Windows 11 File Explorer Styler 1.7.2
entry.content:
• Updated the WindowGlass theme with context menu styling fixes.
  • Background effects are no longer applied for Explorer windows with the legacy frame and for the legacy Control Panel. It was never supported, and previous versions styled only some of the elements in these cases, resulting in a bad experience. If you want background effects for these windows, you might want to try the Translucent Windows mod.

entry.title: Remove Shortcut Arrow Overlays 1.0.0
entry.content:
Remove Shortcut Arrow Overlays

Removes the shortcut arrow overlay from desktop and File Explorer icons cleanly in memory without modifying the Windows Registry.

Why this is better than the Registry tweak:

  • In-Place Overlay Replacement: Modifies Explorer's system image lists in-place with zero image slot leaks.
  • No Black Squares: The common registry tweak (Shell Icons\29 pointing to a blank .ico) frequently causes visual bugs such as black squares on icons after icon cache updates or on high-DPI displays.
  • No Registry Tampering: Does not alter system registry keys and does not require copying files into C:\Windows\System32.
  • Zero Dependencies: Generates a 100% transparent icon dynamically in memory. No external .ico files are needed.
  • Instant Reversibility: Automatically restores the original Windows shortcut arrows when the mod is disabled or unloaded without an Explorer restart.
  • Optional Custom Icon: Allows using a custom badge or icon instead of a completely transparent one.

Scope & Process Behavior

  • System image lists are per-process, so this mod targets explorer.exe (Desktop and File Explorer). Shell Open/Save dialogs hosted inside other application processes retain their separate process image lists.

Credits

  • Credit to the Hide Desktop Icon Text and Shortcut Arrows mod (hide-desktop-icon-text) by kivsak for the transparent GDI icon generation and shell image list technique.

entry.title: Windows 7/8.1 Alt+Tab Recreation 1.0.0
entry.content:
Windows 7/8.1 Alt+Tab Recreation

Windows 7

Windows 8.1

This mod recreates the Windows 7 and the Windows 8.1 Alt+Tab switchers on Windows 10 and Windows 11, with live previews of the windows. It runs in its own process and does not modify explorer.exe.

What it does

  • Draws the switcher the way Windows 7 or Windows 8.1 drew it; the style is chosen in the settings.
  • Shows a live preview of every window, minimized windows included.
  • Shows the icon of the application in the corner of every preview.
  • Draws the Windows 7 panel as Aero glass and the Windows 8.1 one as the solid band it was.
  • Does not page: the previews shrink until every window fits, as the originals did.
  • Does not touch explorer.exe and does not ask for an Explorer restart.
  • If the switcher cannot be shown, Alt+Tab keeps working as usual.

Requirements

  • Windows 10 or Windows 11, 64-bit. The mod was tested on Windows 11 24H2 and on Windows 11 25H2.
  • Windhawk installed, with windhawk.exe not excluded.

How to use

  1. Install the mod in Windhawk and enable it.
  2. Press Alt+Tab. The switcher appears in the style chosen in the settings.
  3. To remove it, disable or uninstall the mod.

Keyboard shortcuts

| Shortcut | Action | | --- | --- | | Alt+Tab, Alt+Shift+Tab | Opens the switcher and moves the selection | | Alt (release) | Activates the selected window | | Tab / Shift+Tab, arrow keys, wheel | Moves the selection while open | | Enter / Space / click | Activates the selected window | | Alt+F4 while open | Closes the selected window | | Esc while open | Closes the switcher without switching | | Ctrl+Alt+F11 | Opens or closes the switcher manually (fallback) | | Alt+` | Optional, off by default: windows of the same app only | | Ctrl+Alt+Tab, Win+Tab | Left to Windows | | Ctrl+Shift+Esc | Left to Windows, opens Task Manager |

Styles

  • Windows 7: a glass panel with rounded corners and a light sheen, the name of the selected window above the row, the previews in a row with the application icon in the corner, and a thin double frame around the selected preview. A minimized window shows its application icon.
  • Windows 8.1: a solid colored band with square corners, a white title above the row, and the previews in a row with the application icon inside their bottom right corner. The selected preview has a white frame.

Comparison with other Alt+Tab mods

Windows 7/8.x Alt+Tab Loader (aubymori) loads the original Alt+Tab component of Windows 7 or Windows 8.x. It is the most faithful option, and the hardest to set up: files have to be copied into the system folder, a matching theme has to be prepared, and Explorer has to be restarted when the mod is enabled and again when it is disabled.

Simple Window Switcher (Lone) is a configurable window switcher, built around Windows 10 and 11 style layouts and around other arrangements as well; recreating the Windows 7 or the 8.1 interface is not its purpose.

This mod recreates those two interfaces and nothing else. Configuration is reduced to the style and a few options, and no file has to be copied, no theme prepared and no restart done. It takes some drawing ideas from the Simple Window Switcher, but it works in a different way and its purpose is a narrower one.

Settings

  • Switcher style: Windows 7 or Windows 8.1.
  • Show the switcher on: the primary monitor, the monitor with the cursor, or the monitor of the active window.
  • Panel color: follow the Windows accent color, as both originals did, or use a custom color.
  • Custom accent color: used only when the panel color is set to custom.
  • Glass density: how much the Windows 7 panel hides the desktop behind it.
  • Desktop dimming: how much the desktop behind the switcher is darkened.
  • Only windows of the current virtual desktop: the filter of the originals. Minimized windows are always listed.
  • The Desktop card: the Desktop at the end of the row, as both originals had.
  • Auto-cycle while Alt is held, Mouse navigation, Alt+`, Ctrl+Alt+F11: the optional extras.
  • Blurred glass behind the panel: for the Windows 7 style.
  • Fade the switcher in and out: 250 ms, off by default.

Notes

  • Use one Alt+Tab replacement at a time.
  • The previews are live, not screenshots: they show the window as it is now.
  • The desktop behind the switcher is a still image.
  • Windows 11 tabbed File Explorer windows appear as one item per window.
  • True fullscreen exclusive games may not show the switcher, like other overlay mods.
  • Windows of applications started as administrator can't be listed or activated: the mod runs at the normal permission level, so the system doesn't let it watch the keyboard of those windows and doesn't let it read their icons or close them with Ctrl+Alt+F4. Such a window keeps the system switcher when it has the focus.
  • The mod can't be turned off from inside an elevated window for the same reason: use a normal window.
  • The mod is released under the GPL-2.0 license.

Credits

  • The look of both styles follows the measurements of the two original switchers.
  • AdministratoX for testing the mod on Windows 11 25H2.

entry.title: Windows 8.1 Start Screen Recreation 1.0.0
entry.content:
Windows 8.1 Start Screen Recreation

This mod recreates the Windows 8.1 Start Screen on Windows 10 and Windows 11.

About the mod

The mod replaces the Start experience with a full-screen Start screen modeled after Windows 8.1: tiles arranged in groups, an All Apps view, type-to-search, and the corresponding menus and animations. Feedback and suggestions are accepted. The mod has been tested on Windows 10 21H2, Windows 10 22H2, Windows 11 24H2 and Windows 11 25H2.

Note: This is a best-effort modification. Layout, colors, icons and animations are inspired by Windows 8.1. Tiles display the real Windows 10/11 applications, so certain original elements (such as Live Tiles and Metro apps) cannot be restored. The mod does not replace system files.

Features

  • Tiles: all four sizes (small, medium, wide, large). Tiles can be dragged, apps can be pinned and unpinned, and groups can be named via right-click on empty space and Name groups.
  • 8.1 menus: right-clicking a tile opens the Windows 8.1 Update menu with the cascading Resize submenu. The bottom command bar (touch / keyboard) provides Advanced, Run, Resize and Unpin.
  • Search: typing starts a search. The search charm covers apps, settings and files, with the Everywhere / Apps / Settings / Files scopes.
  • All Apps view: accessed via the circle arrow at the bottom left; sortable by name, date installed or category.
  • Real tile colors: packaged apps use their own tile color and artwork; classic programs that declare a tile color (such as Chrome) use it as well.
  • Background options: the classic petal artwork, a solid color, the accent color, the desktop wallpaper, or a custom image.
  • Optional 8.1-style layout: modern versions of the old Windows 8.1 apps (Outlook, Calendar, Photos, Weather, and others) can be pinned automatically when installed. Disabled by default; it can be enabled in the settings.

Keyboard shortcuts

| Shortcut | Action | | --- | --- | | Windows key / Start button | Opens or closes Start | | Typing | Starts a search | | Ctrl+Tab | Opens the All Apps view | | Arrow keys + Enter | Navigates and opens apps | | Esc | Closes menus / Start |

Additional information

  • The mod is compatible with the Windows 8/8.1 Charms Bar Recreation and the Windows 8/8.1 Search Charm Recreation mods for a complete Windows 8.1 experience.
  • The mod is available in English, Italian, Spanish, French and Portuguese. The language follows the Windows display language.
  • All options are documented on the mod's settings page in Windhawk.
  • If the Start hook cannot be installed (for example on an unsupported Windows build), the mod falls back to keyboard interception. A lone Windows key press is then detected by a keyboard hook, and the mod sends a synthetic key press of an unassigned key (VK 0xE8) so that Explorer does not open its own Start menu as well.

Credits

  • AdmnistratoX - for the original Windows 8 (8045) Start Screen mod on which this mod is based.
  • WinBoeing 777 - Testing on Windows 10 22H2
  • All testers who reported bugs and provided feedback.

Notes

  • This modification is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Microsoft. entry.title: Top Taskbar Bleed 1.0.0
entry.content:
Top Taskbar Bleed

When a maximized window sits under a top-docked taskbar, the taskbar gets a full-width color panel behind its buttons that matches the window's top edge (optionally as a gradient, for Mica title bars), so the window's title bar appears to continue up into the bar.

Requires a taskbar docked at the top of the screen (via the taskbar position setting on builds that have it, or a mod such as Taskbar on top for Windows 11). On other dock positions this mod stays idle.

How it works:

  • A tracker thread watches window events and finds, per monitor, the foremost maximized window (the first maximized window in z-order on that monitor - not necessarily the foreground window, so a small dialog on top of a maximized app doesn't cancel the bleed).
  • The window's top edge row is captured from the screen and reduced to its dominant color (so a bit of text or an icon can't skew it); that color is the panel and decides the taskbar theme. Pixels covered by another window - a flyout, a thumbnail, a tooltip, a dialog near the top edge - are left out, so floating windows never tint the bleed. Hovering a taskbar thumbnail (Aero Peek) bleeds the peeked window if it is maximized on that monitor and hides the panel otherwise, since the desktop is what shows through.
  • Experimental Gradient bleed: instead of one color, the dominant colors of four windows at 20/40/60/80% of the width - away from the app icon on the left, the caption buttons on the right and a centered title - become a horizontal gradient, so a Mica or gradient title bar continues into the bar (a flat one stays flat). A point that doesn't fit the rest (a toolbar reaching that far, a hovered control) is bridged from its neighbors. Off by default: apps that put content along their very top edge can still show it.
  • One panel per taskbar is inserted into the taskbar's XAML tree, above the taskbar background and below the buttons. The panel mirrors the edge: window changes (switching, maximizing, minimizing) are picked up from window events and applied on the next composed frame, and the edge is re-sampled in between - every Poll interval (250 ms by default) while it is static, every 25 ms while it is changing - so a title bar that recolors in place (focus fade, tab switch, app theme change) is followed frame by frame. With Windows animations on, a window being zoomed into place isn't committed until its edge has actually landed, so the panel never flashes the background behind it; with animations off the first sample is applied as is.

Supports multiple monitors (each taskbar follows its own monitor).

Settings: Poll interval (how often a static edge is re-checked; window changes are event-driven regardless), Excluded programs (executables whose windows should never trigger the bleed) and the experimental Gradient bleed toggle described above.

The panel is a regular XAML Border named TaskbarBleedPanel, so its shape can be styled with Windows 11 Taskbar Styler like any other taskbar element. Target Border#TaskbarBleedPanel and set, for example, Margin=4,4,4,0 or CornerRadius=8,8,0,0 (the panel's bottom edge meets the window, so the rounded corners are normally the top ones). Leave Background and Opacity alone - the mod drives those (the background is a gradient brush).

Notes

  • The taskbar's XAML tree is reached through taskbar.dll and Taskbar.View.dll symbols (downloaded by Windhawk on first run), not through XAML diagnostics, so the mod coexists with Windows 11 Taskbar Styler and other XAML-diagnostics consumers. The bleed applies as soon as the mod is enabled.
  • Cost: with a maximized window present, each poll is one small screen readback (a 1px-high strip) plus a window enumeration; it doesn't register in Task Manager at either rate, and the fast rate only runs during a transition. With no maximized window the poll timer is off, and window events are only acted on when they come from a maximized window or the window being followed, so tooltips, thumbnails and overlays cost nothing.
  • Windows that exclude themselves from capture (protected media, some remote-desktop clients) return no usable pixels; the panel then keeps its last color.
  • The 1px taskbar border line (BackgroundStroke) breaks the illusion; it is hidden while a panel is showing and restored when the panel hides.
  • Readability: a light title bar bled into a dark-mode taskbar leaves white labels on a light panel (and vice versa). While a panel is showing, the mod switches that monitor's taskbar to the theme that matches the bled color (light panel -> light mode, dark panel -> dark mode) and restores the previous theme when the panel hides. This is done per taskbar through XAML's RequestedTheme, so only the affected monitor changes and the system theme itself is untouched.

Credits

The taskbar-thread helpers (RunFromWindowThread, FindCurrentProcessTaskbarWnd) and the taskbar.dll XAML-root lookup are ported from Taskbar multi-row by m417z, licensed under the GNU GPL v3.0. This mod is published under the same license.

entry.title: Drag to Scroll 1.0.0
entry.content:
Drag to Scroll

Hold Ctrl + Right-Click and drag your mouse to scroll smoothly and naturally across desktop applications, including web browsers (Chrome, Edge, Firefox), text editors (VS Code, Notepad++), File Explorer, and legacy Win32 utilities.

Key Features

  • High-Resolution Micro-Scrolling: Injects fractional wheel increments for fluid, trackpad-like scrolling in modern desktop apps and web browsers.
  • Legacy Control Detection: Automatically detects classic Win32 controls (e.g., standard list views, tree views, edit boxes) and routes discrete WM_VSCROLL line steps to preserve native line-by-line movement.
  • Hands-Free Cruising: Release the Right Mouse Button while continuing to hold Ctrl to let the page cruise automatically based on cursor offset. Cruising disengages instantly on keypress, mouse click, or Ctrl release.
  • Zero Zoom Interference: Dynamically masks Ctrl state during scroll dispatch so applications never accidentally trigger browser zoom or editor scaling.
  • Accidental Click Protection: Tapping Ctrl + Right-Click in place without exceeding the deadzone transparently passes through as a regular right-click.

Compatibility & Limitations

  • Packaged & Modern UI Surfaces: Certain modern Windows interfaces (such as the Windows Start Menu or some packaged store apps) do not process standard Win32 mouse-drag messages through the message queue and are not supported.
  • CAD & 3D Software: If you use software (such as Blender, AutoCAD, or video games) that natively binds actions to Ctrl + Right-Click, you can exclude those executables under the mod's Advanced tab in Windhawk.

entry.title: Live Update for Windows 11 2.0.206
entry.content:
Live Update for Windows 11

A unified, single-slot "Live Activity" widget injected natively into the primary Windows 11 XAML taskbar. Instead of running multiple separate taskbar widgets or external desktop overlay windows, Live Update multiplexes contextual activities into one compact taskbar slot with a native XAML flyout popup.

Overview: Media

Overview: RAM Alert

Overview: Device Battery & Bluetooth Battery

Overview: Sensitive Permission

Overview: Wi-Fi Hotspot

How this mod differs from existing mods

  • Native single-slot multiplexer vs. external overlays: Unlike Dynamic Island for Windows (which runs as a separate overlay window at the top of the screen), this mod embeds directly inside the native Windows 11 taskbar layout (SystemTrayFrameGrid / RootGrid) and shares a single compact slot across all active providers.
  • Contextual activity switching vs. single-purpose widgets: Unlike standalone media mods (Taskbar Music Lounge, Taskbar Fluent Media Player, Island Media Controls) or calendar-only mods (Lunar & Holiday Calendar), this widget automatically switches to newly started activities (such as media playback, power connection, timer start, or microphone/camera access) while keeping a Vietnamese lunar calendar & almanac as the idle baseline.

Features

  • Media: Shows album artwork, track title, artist, interactive seek bar, and Fluent transport controls for players integrated with Windows Global System Media Transport Controls (GSMTC), with session switching for up to 16 active sessions.
  • Battery & Bluetooth: Displays charge percentage, charging/discharging state, estimated remaining/full time, connected Bluetooth device battery levels, and a shortcut to Windows Power & battery settings (ms-settings:powersleep).
  • Windows Clock (status reader): Displays active Stopwatch, Timer, and enabled Alarm entries observed from the Windows Clock app, continuing to advance locally from the last synced state when the app is minimized.
  • Lunar Calendar, Almanac & Vietnamese Culture Index: Computes UTC+7 Vietnamese lunar dates, Can Chi, Nạp Âm, auspicious hours (Giờ Hoàng Đạo), and 12 Trực using the Hồ Ngọc Đức algorithm. Includes a monthly calendar view, Vietnamese holiday list, and a built-in Vietnamese culture topic index that opens reference articles in your default browser.
  • Privacy Activity: Passively monitors active Microphone (Core Audio), Camera (Media Foundation sensor monitor), and Location usage and lists the reporting applications.
  • Task Progress: Passively observes taskbar progress (ITaskbarList3) for File Explorer, browsers, and archivers to display ongoing transfers in one place.
  • Displays & Wi-Fi Hotspot: Shows active external monitors/projection mode (QueryDisplayConfig) and Windows Mobile Hotspot status/connected client count (NetworkOperatorTetheringManager).
  • System Alerts (RAM & Storage on by default; Temperature optional, off by default):
  • RAM & Storage (enabled by default): Alerts when physical RAM crosses 80%/90%/95% or when any fixed drive has less than 10% free space (listing the low-space volumes).
  • CPU/GPU Temperature (optional, off by default): Alerts when CPU/GPU temperatures from a local LibreHardwareMonitor web server (http://127.0.0.1:<port>/data.json) cross 70/80/90 °C.
  • OBS Studio Recording (optional, off by default): Connects to local OBS WebSocket v5 (ws://127.0.0.1:<port>) when OBS is running to display recording elapsed time and Pause/Resume/Stop buttons.

Quick toggles, positioning & notes

  • Taskbar position (root_left on centered taskbar, automatic tray_left on left-aligned taskbar): By default (root_left), when the Windows 11 taskbar is centered, the widget sits on the left side of the taskbar right after the native Windows Widgets button (or at the left edge if Widgets is turned off in Windows Settings). You can optionally enable Hide Windows Widgets button in left corner (appearance.hideWidgetsButton, off by default) to collapse the native Widgets button while using root_left and restore its original state when disabled. Whenever the taskbar is left-aligned (TaskbarAl = 0), root_left automatically falls back to the system tray (tray_left) so the Start button and app icons are never covered.
  • Right-click quick toggles vs. Windhawk settings: Toggles in the widget's right-click context menu save quick runtime overrides (ui.*) that take precedence over the Windhawk settings tab. Saving settings in Windhawk (or choosing Reset to Windhawk settings in the context menu) clears all runtime overrides.
  • OBS WebSocket password: The obs.password field is stored as a standard Windhawk mod setting, so it is included in Windhawk settings exports.

Optional local integrations setup

  • OBS Studio: Enable Tools > WebSocket Server Settings > Enable WebSocket server in OBS Studio (v28+), then enable OBS recording in the mod settings and match the port (default 4455) and password.
  • LibreHardwareMonitor (Temperature): In LibreHardwareMonitor, enable Options > Remote Web Server > Run, then enable Temperature alerts in the mod settings and match the local port (default 8085).

Compatibility

  • Supported OS: Windows 11 (build 22000 or later) with the native primary XAML taskbar.
  • Windows 10 and third-party replacement taskbars are not supported.

Tiếng Việt

Live Update for Windows 11 tích hợp nhiều hoạt động trực tiếp (Live Activities) vào một vị trí duy nhất trên thanh taskbar gốc của Windows 11.

Điểm khác biệt so với các mod hiện có

  • Tích hợp trực tiếp vào taskbar thay vì cửa sổ nổi: Khác với Dynamic Island for Windows (tạo cửa sổ nổi riêng phía trên màn hình), mod này gắn trực tiếp vào cây giao diện XAML của taskbar Windows 11 và dùng chung một ô hiển thị duy nhất.
  • Tự động chuyển đổi theo ngữ cảnh: Khác với các mod chỉ hiển thị nhạc hoặc chỉ hiển thị âm lịch, Live Update tự động ưu tiên hoạt động mới phát sinh (như phát nhạc, cắm sạc, bật hẹn giờ, dùng micro/camera, quay OBS) và hiển thị Âm lịch & Tử vi khi ở trạng thái nghỉ.

Các hoạt động hỗ trợ

  • Phương tiện (Media): Ảnh bìa, tên bài hát, nghệ sĩ, thanh tua và nút điều khiển nhạc hỗ trợ nhiều phiên phát cùng lúc.
  • Pin & Thiết bị Bluetooth: Phần trăm pin, thời gian ước tính, mức pin thiết bị Bluetooth đang kết nối và nút mở nhanh cài đặt Nguồn & Pin của Windows.
  • Đồng hồ Windows: Đọc trạng thái Bấm giờ, Hẹn giờ và Báo thức từ ứng dụng Đồng hồ Windows; tiếp tục đếm từ mốc đồng bộ cuối khi thu nhỏ ứng dụng.
  • Âm lịch, Tử vi & Danh mục Văn hóa Việt: Tính ngày âm lịch, Can Chi, Nạp Âm, Giờ Hoàng Đạo, Trực, lịch tháng và danh sách ngày lễ Việt Nam. Mục Văn hóa cung cấp danh mục chủ đề văn hóa Việt Nam và mở bài viết tham khảo trong trình duyệt mặc định khi bấm vào.
  • Quyền riêng tư: Hiển thị ứng dụng đang sử dụng Micro, Camera hoặc Vị trí.
  • Tiến trình tác vụ: Theo dõi trạng thái tiến độ trên taskbar của File Explorer, trình duyệt và phần mềm giải nén.
  • Trình chiếu & Điểm phát sóng Wi-Fi: Hiển thị màn hình phụ đang kết nối và trạng thái Mobile Hotspot cùng danh sách thiết bị.
  • Cảnh báo hệ thống (RAM & Bộ nhớ bật mặc định; Nhiệt độ tùy chọn, tắt mặc định):
  • RAM & Ổ đĩa (bật mặc định): Cảnh báo khi RAM vượt 80%/90%/95% hoặc khi ổ đĩa cố định còn dưới 10% dung lượng trống (hiển thị rõ tên ổ đĩa bị đầy).
  • Nhiệt độ CPU/GPU (tùy chọn, tắt mặc định): Cảnh báo khi nhiệt độ CPU/GPU đọc từ LibreHardwareMonitor Remote Web Server (http://127.0.0.1:<port>/data.json) vượt 70/80/90 °C.
  • Quay màn hình OBS (tùy chọn, tắt mặc định): Kết nối cục bộ (127.0.0.1) với OBS WebSocket v5 khi bật trong cài đặt để hiển thị thời lượng quay và nút Tạm dừng/Tiếp tục/Dừng.

Lưu ý về vị trí, menu chuột phải & mật khẩu OBS

  • Vị trí mặc định (root_left khi taskbar căn giữa, tự động về tray_left khi taskbar căn trái): Mặc định khi thanh taskbar Windows 11 căn giữa, widget nằm ở góc trái (root_left) ngay sau nút Các tiện ích (Widgets) của Windows để không chồng lấp (hoặc sát mép trái nếu bạn đã tắt Widgets trong cài đặt Windows). Bạn có thể bật tùy chọn Ẩn nút Các tiện ích (Widgets) ở góc trái (appearance.hideWidgetsButton, tắt mặc định) nếu muốn ẩn nút Widgets gốc khi dùng root_left (tự khôi phục đúng trạng thái ban đầu khi tắt). Khi thanh taskbar được căn trái (TaskbarAl = 0), mod sẽ tự động chuyển vị trí về khay hệ thống (tray_left) để không bao giờ đè lên nút Start và các biểu tượng ứng dụng.
  • Menu chuột phải và cài đặt Windhawk: Các tùy chọn bật/tắt nhanh trong menu chuột phải lưu trạng thái ghi đè tạm thời (ui.*) và được ưu tiên hơn trang cài đặt Windhawk. Khi bạn bấm Lưu trong trang cài đặt Windhawk (hoặc chọn Khôi phục theo cài đặt Windhawk trong menu chuột phải), các ghi đè tạm thời này sẽ được xóa.
  • Mật khẩu OBS WebSocket: Trường obs.password là cài đặt thông thường của Windhawk nên sẽ được bao gồm khi xuất (export) cài đặt Windhawk.

entry.title: Windows 11 Notification Center Styler 1.8

entry.title: Windows Key to Search 1.0
entry.content:
Windows Key to Search

Tap either Windows key to open Search instead of Start. Search opens when the key is released. Windows-key combinations such as Win+E, Win+R, Win+Shift+S, and Win+S continue to work normally. The generated shortcut is held for 50 ms before release.

By default, the helper runs without requesting administrator privileges. On Windhawk 1.7.3, administrator windows keep their normal Windows-key behavior. On Windhawk 2.0 alpha 4 or later, the mod requests UIAccess, which also covers administrator windows when that host is available.

The optional Support administrator windows on Windhawk 1.7.3 setting launches an elevated helper. It is off by default. Enabling it can show a UAC prompt at every sign-in, and after enabling or updating the mod. The prompt runs on a background thread, and an already-running helper prevents another prompt. If elevation is cancelled, the helper runs normally instead. Disable and re-enable the mod after changing this setting. On Windhawk 2.0, leave this setting off and use its UIAccess host.

The helper uses Windhawk's tool-mod launcher, with an optional background elevation path on older Windhawk versions.

Windows-key mouse gestures used by tools such as AltDrag or AltSnap are not supported: the mod withholds the Windows key until another keyboard key is pressed. UAC's secure desktop is outside the scope of the mod.

entry.title: TopBar for Windows 1.4.1
entry.content:
Addition:

  • Added a Shortcuts panel in the Settings app to assign custom keyboard shortcuts for flyouts, Start, Search, and Restart Explorer, including support for overriding Windows default keys.
  • Added Titlebar Bleed: When a window is maximized, the TopBar now samples the maximized window's titlebar gradient and displays it behind the bar's content.

Updates:

  • Fixed the Top Bar not hiding in full screen window.
  • Fixed the Auto-Hide animation causing the Top Bar to misalign to the top-left.
  • Fixed TopBar popup is misaligned at top left, and is rendering small when secondary is set to Vertical Alignment.

  • Now, setting Width=Auto for Grid#TopBarRoot makes combine removes space between Left, Right, and Center panel and topbar looks like a dynamic island instead of a Bar.
  • Fixed GreenBar theme not applying custom colors to WinUI3 icons.

entry.title: Minecraft launcher region detection spoof 0.1.0
entry.content:
Minecraft launcher region detection spoof

Presents Singapore region information to PCL CE and HMCL to bypass their mainland China restrictions on downloading, installing and repairing Minecraft. The purpose is to give users the same choice of launcher features across regions.

Region and time zone

  • PCL CE: user region SG, Windows device region GeoID 215, and Singapore Standard Time.
  • HMCL: Windows user GeoID 215, JVM country SG, and JVM time zone Asia/Singapore. Existing user.country and user.timezone JVM options are replaced, and legacy user.region options are removed.
  • The affected launcher's time zone is fixed to UTC+8, without daylight saving time. Local times shown by the launcher use UTC+8 even when Windows is set to another time zone.
  • Language settings are preserved. Locale-dependent formats can reflect the Singapore region. The overrides apply within the target processes.

Target processes

Supports 64-bit x64 and ARM64 processes with these executable names:

  • PCL2_CE*.exe for PCL CE.
  • HMCL*.exe for HMCL executables.
  • java.exe and javaw.exe when the command line launches HMCL*.jar, a JAR embedded in HMCL*.exe, or the main class org.jackhuang.hmcl.Main.

Usage

Enable the mod before starting HMCL so that its region options are set before JVM creation. Restart PCL CE after enabling the mod to refresh its cached region and local time zone. To restore the original region behavior, disable the mod and fully restart the affected launcher.

Upstream changes

  • PCL CE #3673 introduces mainland China restrictions for Minecraft and modpack downloads, installation and repair, using Windows region, locale, language and time zone signals.
  • PCL CE #3676 adds the Windows device region as an additional detection signal.
  • HMCL #7017 introduces mainland China restrictions for game downloads.
